title: The History of Everything: From the Big Bang to Today
length_note: 63 classes of 30 minutes each, so about 31.5 hours in all. The length is fixed at 30 minutes because that was requested. It also suits learners who tire easily or are relearning, because each class covers one idea or one era. The count follows the story. Classes 1-13 cover the universe, Earth, life and early humans. Classes 14-20 cover farming, the first cities and the Bronze and Iron Ages. Classes 21-35 cover the classical and medieval worlds on every inhabited continent, so that Europe is not treated as the whole story. Classes 36-49 cover the early modern and 19th-century world. Classes 50-62 cover the 20th century to today. Class 63 looks ahead. Each class has a frame-of-reference segment (science, politics, art and notable people from the same time) and a segment on where experts disagree. The Holocaust gets its own class and a content note. Because the course is ongoing, it can be built a few classes at a time in order. Every class needs its facts researched and sourced before it is written.

classes.title: How Do We Know? Reading the Evidence and Telling Time
classes.goal: Explain how scientists and historians date things and why the course uses 'frames of reference'.
topics: Scales of time from billions of years to a single year
Dating methods: radiometric dating, tree rings, written records
Difference between evidence, interpretation and debate
How to use a same-time snapshot

classes.title: The Big Bang and the First Minutes
classes.goal: Describe in plain words what the Big Bang model says and what evidence supports it.
topics: Expansion of the universe and the cosmic microwave background
Debate: what, if anything, came before; inflation and alternative models
Frame of reference: how and when this was discovered, and who by

classes.title: First Stars, Galaxies and the Making of the Elements
classes.goal: Explain how stars made the elements that later formed planets and people.
topics: Open questions: dark matter and dark energy
Frame of reference: telescopes and discoveries that revealed this

classes.title: Our Sun and Solar System
classes.goal: Say how the Sun and planets formed and roughly when.
topics: Debate: migration of the giant planets
Frame of reference: age of the solar system compared with the age of the universe

classes.title: Early Earth and the Moon
classes.goal: Describe the young Earth and the leading explanation for the Moon's origin.

classes.title: The Origin of Life
classes.goal: Explain the main ideas for how life began and say why the question is still open.
topics: Earliest fossil and chemical evidence of life
Hypotheses: hydrothermal vents, warm pools, RNA world
What we do and don't know

classes.title: Complex Cells, Oxygen and a Changing Planet
classes.goal: Describe how oxygen and complex cells changed Earth.
topics: Photosynthesis and the Great Oxidation Event
Debate: how severe the glaciations were

classes.title: Animals Appear: The Cambrian to Life on Land
classes.goal: Trace how animals, plants and fungi came to fill the seas and then the land.
topics: Debate: how sudden the Cambrian explosion really was

classes.title: Extinctions, Dinosaurs and the Rise of Mammals
classes.goal: Name the major mass extinctions and explain what ended the age of dinosaurs.

classes.title: From Primates to Early Hominins
classes.goal: Explain how the human line separated from other apes.
topics: Debate: where and why upright walking evolved

classes.title: The Genus Homo: Neanderthals, Denisovans and Us
classes.goal: Describe our species and its close relatives, and how we know about them.
topics: Origins of Homo sapiens in Africa
Debate: 'Out of Africa' versus multiregional models

classes.title: Ice Age Minds: Fire, Tools, Language and Art
classes.goal: Describe what early humans made and the debates about when modern thinking began.
topics: Stone tools and control of fire

classes.title: People Spread Across the Planet
classes.goal: Outline how people reached every continent except Antarctica.
topics: Debate: when and how people reached the Americas
Megafauna extinctions and the debate over human causes

classes.title: The Farming Revolution
classes.goal: Explain what farming changed and the theories about why it began.
topics: Ice Age end and the Holocene
Early crops and animals in several regions
Debate: why farming began and whether it improved life

classes.title: The First Cities and the Invention of Writing
classes.goal: Say where and when the first cities and writing appeared and what they were used for.
topics: Frame of reference: other regions in the same centuries

classes.title: Egypt and the Indus Valley
classes.goal: Compare two early river civilizations.
topics: Undeciphered Indus script and debate over its meaning
Debate: why the Indus cities declined

classes.title: The Bronze Age World and Its Collapse
classes.goal: Describe the connected Bronze Age societies and the theories for their end.
topics: Minoans, Mycenaeans, Hittites, New Kingdom Egypt
Debate: causes of the Late Bronze Age collapse

classes.title: Other Early Worlds: Africa, the Americas and the Pacific
classes.goal: Show that complex societies were arising on every inhabited continent.

classes.title: Iron Age Empires: Assyria, Babylon and Persia
classes.goal: Explain how large empires were built and governed.
topics: Debate: how to use religious texts as historical evidence

classes.title: Thinkers and Teachers: Buddha, Confucius, the Greeks and the Prophets
classes.goal: Describe major philosophies and religions of the first millennium BCE and the debate over a shared 'Axial Age'.
topics: Debate: was there really an 'Axial Age'?

classes.title: Classical Greece
classes.goal: Explain Greek city-states, democracy and Greek contributions to art and science.
topics: Persian Wars and the Peloponnesian War
Limits of Athenian democracy: who was excluded

classes.title: Alexander and the Hellenistic World
classes.goal: Describe Alexander's conquests and their long-term effects.

classes.title: The Rise of Rome
classes.goal: Explain how Rome grew from a city to a Mediterranean power.
topics: Julius Caesar and the end of the Republic

classes.title: Mauryan India, Qin and Han China
classes.goal: Compare how India and China built their first large empires.
topics: Qin unification and the First Emperor
Han dynasty, bureaucracy and invention of paper
Compare with Rome in the same centuries

classes.title: The Roman Empire, the Silk Roads and Early Christianity
classes.goal: Describe the connected Eurasian world around the year 1 CE.
topics: Silk Road and Indian Ocean trade
Debate: how many people lived in the Roman Empire and how we estimate

classes.title: Late Antiquity: Changing Empires
classes.goal: Explain the competing explanations for Rome's western decline and what else was changing.

classes.title: The Rise of Islam and the Caliphates
classes.goal: Describe how Islam began and spread and what the early caliphates were like.
topics: Debate: early Islamic sources and how historians use them

classes.title: Byzantium, Early Medieval Europe and the Vikings
classes.goal: Describe the post-Roman West and the Byzantine East.
topics: Debate: were the 'Dark Ages' really dark?

classes.title: Tang and Song China and the Islamic Golden Age
classes.goal: Describe two great centers of science, trade and invention.
topics: House of Wisdom, algebra, medicine and optics
Debate: how much was 'Golden Age' and how much was borrowed or shared

classes.title: Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia and Medieval India
classes.goal: Place the societies of East, Southeast and South Asia on the map of the medieval world.
topics: Heian Japan and later samurai rule

classes.title: Medieval Africa: Ghana, Mali, Great Zimbabwe and the Swahili Coast
classes.goal: Describe African kingdoms and trade networks in the Middle Ages.
topics: Debate: how to interpret oral and archaeological evidence

classes.title: The Americas and Pacific Before 1492
classes.goal: Describe the major societies of the Americas and Pacific before European contact.
topics: Polynesian navigation and settlement of Aotearoa/New Zealand

classes.title: High Medieval Europe: Crusades, Castles and Universities
classes.goal: Explain feudal society, the Crusades and the growth of towns and learning.
topics: Feudalism: how useful is the term?

classes.title: The Mongol Empire
classes.goal: Explain how the Mongols built the largest land empire and what it changed.
topics: Pax Mongolica and exchange across Eurasia
Debate: destruction versus connection in the legacy

classes.title: The Black Death and the Crisis of the 1300s
classes.goal: Describe the plague and its effects on societies.
topics: Death toll estimates and the debate over them

classes.title: The Renaissance
classes.goal: Describe what changed in art, ideas and technology in Europe from the 1300s to 1500s.
topics: Debate: was the Renaissance a break with the Middle Ages?

classes.title: Ottomans, Ming China and the Age of Exploration
classes.goal: Explain why Europeans, Chinese and others made long sea voyages and what came of them.
topics: Portuguese routes along Africa and to Asia
Debate: why China stopped its treasure voyages

classes.title: Contact and the Columbian Exchange
classes.goal: Describe the effects of Europe–Americas contact on people, crops, animals and disease.
topics: Conquest of the Aztec and Inca empires
Disease and population collapse: size and causes debated
Spread of crops such as potatoes, maize and sugar

classes.title: The Reformation and the Wars of Religion
classes.goal: Explain how Christianity split in Western Europe and what followed.
topics: Religious change elsewhere in the world

classes.title: The Scientific Revolution
classes.goal: Describe how new methods and discoveries changed thinking about nature.

classes.title: The Atlantic Slave Trade
classes.goal: Explain how the trade worked, its scale and its lasting effects.
topics: Debate: economic effects on Europe, the Americas and Africa
Content note: the subject is painful

classes.title: Mughal, Safavid, Qing and Tokugawa: Early Modern Asia
classes.goal: Compare the great Asian states of the 1500s–1700s.

classes.title: Enlightenment and Absolute Monarchy
classes.goal: Describe the clash between royal power and new ideas about rights and reason.
topics: English Civil War and Glorious Revolution
Locke, Voltaire, Rousseau, and Enlightenment thinkers
Debate: limits of Enlightenment ideals on slavery, gender and empire
Music and art of the era

classes.title: The American and French Revolutions
classes.goal: Explain causes and results of two revolutions and how they spread ideas.
topics: Debate: how revolutionary were they, and for whom?
Frame of reference: other world events 1776–1799

classes.title: Napoleon, Haiti and Latin American Independence
classes.goal: Describe how revolutions and wars remade the Atlantic world.
topics: Bolívar, San Martín and independence movements

classes.title: The Industrial Revolution
classes.goal: Explain what industrialization was and the theories for why it began in Britain.
topics: Debate: why Britain, and why then (the 'Great Divergence')
Environmental effects, early signs of climate change

classes.title: Nations, Reform and Civil War in the 1800s
classes.goal: Describe the rise of nation-states and the movements for rights.

classes.title: Imperialism: Africa, India, China and Japan
classes.goal: Explain how European and other powers expanded their control and how people responded.
topics: British rule in India and the 1857 rebellion
Debate: costs and benefits and how historians weigh them

classes.title: Science and Ideas in the 1800s
classes.goal: Describe major discoveries and how they changed daily life and worldviews.
topics: Debate: reception and misuse of Darwin's ideas

classes.title: The Road to World War I
classes.goal: Explain the long- and short-term causes of the war.
topics: Debate: who or what was responsible
Europe's empires and other parts of the world in 1900–1914

classes.title: World War I
classes.goal: Describe the course, cost and consequences of the war.
topics: Western Front, Eastern Front and wider fronts
Treaty of Versailles and its critics
Casualty figures and how they are estimated

classes.title: Revolution, Flu and the Roaring Twenties
classes.goal: Describe the turbulent years right after 1918.

classes.title: Depression, Dictators and the Slide to War
classes.goal: Explain how economic crisis and extremism changed politics in the 1930s.
topics: Fascism in Italy and Nazism in Germany
Japan's expansion and the war in China
Debate: appeasement and whether war was avoidable

classes.title: World War II
classes.goal: Outline the main theaters of the war and how it ended.
topics: Europe, the Atlantic, the Soviet front
Atomic bombs and the debate over their use
Total deaths and how they are counted

classes.title: The Holocaust and the Memory of Genocide
classes.goal: Explain what the Holocaust was, how it happened and how it is remembered.
topics: Content note: this class covers genocide, written with care
Nazi persecution and mass murder of Jews, and of Roma, disabled people and others
Victims' own voices, including diaries such as Anne Frank's
Nuremberg and the idea of 'genocide' in law

classes.title: A New World Order: The UN, the Cold War and Decolonization
classes.goal: Describe the world that emerged after 1945.
topics: Independence movements in Africa, Asia and the Middle East
Debate: who was responsible for the Cold War

classes.title: The 1950s and early 1960s: Space, Nuclear Fear and Civil Rights
classes.goal: Describe the major events and movements of these years.
topics: Korea and the nuclear arms race

classes.title: The Late 1960s and 1970s: Protest, War and Oil
classes.goal: Describe turbulence and change in these years worldwide.
topics: Debate: how to assess the Cultural Revolution's toll

classes.title: 20th-Century Science and Technology
classes.goal: Explain the big ideas and inventions that changed the century.
topics: Return to the Big Bang: how we learned the story from Class 2

classes.title: The End of the Cold War
classes.goal: Explain how and why the Cold War ended.
topics: 1989 revolutions and fall of the Berlin Wall
Debate: what mattered most — pressure, reform or economics
South Africa and the end of apartheid

classes.title: Globalization, the Internet and a New Century
classes.goal: Describe the changes in the 1990s and 2000s.
topics: The World Wide Web and mobile phones
Rise of China and India's economy
September 11, 2001 and the wars that followed

classes.title: 2008 to Today
classes.goal: Describe major recent events and say why recent history is hard to judge.
topics: Climate change: evidence and policy debates
Why historians are cautious about the very recent past

classes.title: Looking Ahead: The Future of Earth and the Universe
classes.goal: Summarize the whole story and describe what science says about possible futures.
topics: Review: the big turning points from Big Bang to now
Future of the Sun and Earth
Possible fates of the universe, and why they are debated
Choices and uncertainty in human futures
